Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We investigate the possibility of electroweak phase transition in the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) with an extra $U(1)'$. This model has two Higgs doublets and a singlet, in addition to a singlet exotic quark superfield. We find that at the one-loop level this model may accommodate the electroweak phase transitions that are strongly first-order in a reasonably large region of the parameter space. In the parameter region where the phase transitions take place, we observe that the lightest scalar Higgs boson has a smaller mass when the strength of the phase transition becomes weaker. Also, the other three heavier neutral Higgs bosons get more large masses when the strength of the phase transition becomes weaker.

This model contains two Higgs doublets and a singlet, as well as a singlet exotic quark superfield. We find that, at the one-loop level, the model can accommodate strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions within a reasonably large region of parameter space. outputs.L2: We study whether an electroweak phase transition can occur in the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) extended by an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry. The model contains two Higgs doublets and one singlet, as well as a singlet exotic quark superfield. outputs.L3:
The study examines electroweak phase transitions in an extension of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) that includes an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry. Such extensions are motivated by the possibility of addressing shortcomings of the MSSM and can significantly modify the Higgs sector and the thermal evolution of the early universe.

In this model, the Higgs sector contains two Higgs doublets, as in the MSSM, together with an additional singlet field. The singlet plays an important role in generating an effective \(\mu\)-term and in modifying the Higgs potential. The model also includes a singlet exotic quark superfield, which contributes to the one-loop effective potential and can influence the dynamics of the electroweak phase transition.

By analyzing the finite-temperature effective potential at the one-loop level, the study finds that the model can support strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions over a reasonably broad region of parameter space. This is an important result because a strong first-order electroweak phase transition is one of the necessary ingredients for successful electroweak baryogenesis, which aims to explain the observed matter–antimatter asymmetry of the universe.

The behavior of the Higgs spectrum is closely connected to the strength of the phase transition. In the region of parameter space where the phase transition occurs, the lightest scalar Higgs boson tends to have a smaller mass as the transition becomes weaker. This indicates a correlation between the low-energy Higgs spectrum and the thermal history of the model.

Conversely, the three heavier neutral Higgs bosons show the opposite trend. As the strength of the electroweak phase transition weakens, these heavier Higgs states become more massive. Thus, the model predicts a characteristic relationship between the order parameter of the phase transition and the neutral Higgs mass spectrum: weaker transitions are associated with a lighter lightest scalar Higgs boson but heavier additional neutral Higgs bosons.

Overall, the analysis demonstrates that the MSSM extended by an extra \(U(1)'\) symmetry provides a viable framework for achieving strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions at the one-loop level, while also producing distinctive correlations among the masses of the neutral Higgs bosons.
outputs.L4:
This study examines the nature of the electroweak phase transition in a supersymmetric model based on the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model extended by an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry. The model contains two Higgs doublets, as in the MSSM, together with an extra gauge-singlet Higgs field and a singlet exotic quark superfield. Such extensions are motivated in part by their ability to address the \(\mu\)-problem of the MSSM and by the richer Higgs and neutral gauge-boson sectors that arise from the enlarged symmetry structure.

The analysis is carried out by constructing the finite-temperature one-loop effective potential for the scalar fields. This potential is used to study the evolution of the Higgs vacuum expectation values as the temperature decreases in the early universe. In particular, the strength of the electroweak phase transition is evaluated by examining the ratio of the Higgs vacuum expectation value at the critical temperature to the critical temperature itself. A strongly first-order electroweak phase transition is of special interest because it is one of the necessary ingredients for successful electroweak baryogenesis.

The results show that the \(U(1)'\)-extended MSSM can support a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition over a sizable region of parameter space. The presence of the singlet field and its couplings to the Higgs doublets and exotic matter can significantly modify the thermal effective potential, making the transition stronger than in the minimal supersymmetric case for appropriate choices of parameters. This demonstrates that the extended gauge and Higgs structure plays an important role in shaping the finite-temperature behavior of the theory.

A notable feature of the analysis is the correlation between the strength of the phase transition and the Higgs mass spectrum. Parameter regions that produce weaker first-order transitions tend to be associated with a lighter lightest scalar Higgs boson and heavier additional neutral Higgs states. Conversely, stronger transitions are typically connected with different patterns in the neutral Higgs spectrum, reflecting the influence of singlet-doublet mixing and the additional interactions introduced by the \(U(1)'\) symmetry.

Overall, the study indicates that \(U(1)'\)-extended supersymmetric models provide a viable framework for obtaining a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition. The results also suggest that measurements of the Higgs sector, particularly the masses and mixings of the neutral Higgs bosons, could offer important clues about the viability of electroweak baryogenesis in this class of models.
outputs.L5:
The Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) is one of the most studied extensions of the Standard Model of particle physics. This theory introduces supersymmetry, a proposed symmetry between fermions and bosons, and predicts the existence of new partner particles for every known particle.

A key feature of the MSSM is its expanded Higgs sector. Unlike the Standard Model, which contains one Higgs doublet and predicts a single Higgs boson, the MSSM requires two Higgs doublets. This leads to five physical Higgs particles: two neutral CP-even Higgs bosons, one neutral CP-odd Higgs boson, and two charged Higgs bosons.

The discovery of a Higgs boson at CERN in 2012 provided strong support for the mechanism that gives particles mass, but it also opened new questions. In the MSSM, the observed Higgs particle can be interpreted as the lighter CP-even Higgs boson, though this depends on the values of the model’s parameters. Researchers continue to compare MSSM predictions with experimental data to search for signs of supersymmetry and additional Higgs particles.

This ongoing work is important because the MSSM may help address unresolved problems in modern physics, such as the hierarchy problem, dark matter, and the unification of forces. While no direct evidence for supersymmetric particles has yet been confirmed, the MSSM remains a powerful framework for exploring physics beyond the Standard Model.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a physics paper studying the electroweak phase transition in the MSSM extended by an extra U(1)' gauge symmetry, including the Higgs sector, one-loop effects, and Higgs mass behavior.
counterfactuals.output:
We investigate the electroweak phase transition in a supersymmetric model based on the MSSM extended by an additional Abelian gauge symmetry, \(U(1)'\). The enlarged gauge structure modifies the Higgs sector through new \(D\)-term contributions and the presence of an additional singlet field, which can generate an effective \(\mu\) parameter after symmetry breaking. We analyze the finite-temperature effective potential including the tree-level scalar potential, one-loop zero-temperature radiative corrections, and thermal contributions from the relevant bosonic and fermionic degrees of freedom. Particular attention is paid to the role of the extended Higgs sector in strengthening the electroweak phase transition and to the dependence of the critical temperature and order parameter on the model parameters.

We show that the extra \(U(1)'\) interactions and singlet-induced couplings can significantly alter the vacuum structure relative to the MSSM, allowing regions of parameter space where a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition is realized. The one-loop corrections, especially those associated with the top/stop sector and the extended Higgs spectrum, play an important role in determining both the strength of the transition and the stability of the electroweak vacuum. We also study the behavior of the Higgs masses as functions of the singlet vacuum expectation value, soft supersymmetry-breaking parameters, and the additional gauge coupling. The lightest Higgs mass receives sizable tree-level and radiative contributions, relaxing the tension present in the MSSM and permitting phenomenologically viable spectra consistent with electroweak symmetry breaking.

Our results demonstrate that \(U(1)'\)-extended supersymmetric models provide a natural framework in which the Higgs mass constraints and the requirements for a strong electroweak phase transition can be simultaneously addressed. This makes such models promising candidates for electroweak baryogenesis and motivates further phenomenological studies of their Higgs and gauge sectors.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a research result about strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions in a U(1)'-extended MSSM with two Higgs doublets, a singlet, and exotic quark superfields.
counterfactuals.output:
A key research result for a \(U(1)'\)-extended MSSM is that it can naturally realize a **strongly first-order electroweak phase transition**, suitable for electroweak baryogenesis, more easily than the ordinary MSSM.

In this class of models, the Higgs sector contains

\[
H_d,\quad H_u,\quad S,
\]

where \(S\) is a Standard Model singlet charged under the extra \(U(1)'\). The superpotential typically includes

\[
W \supset h_s S H_u H_d + h_Q S Q \bar Q ,
\]

so that the singlet generates an effective \(\mu\)-term,

\[
\mu_{\rm eff}=h_s \langle S\rangle ,
\]

and also gives mass to exotic quark superfields \(Q,\bar Q\).

The important result is that the extra singlet and \(U(1)'\) interactions modify the finite-temperature Higgs potential in a way that strengthens the electroweak phase transition. In particular:

- the singlet-Higgs coupling \(h_s S H_uH_d\) introduces additional tree-level structure in the scalar potential;
- exotic quarks and squarks can give sizable thermal loop corrections;
- the extra \(U(1)'\) \(D\)-terms increase the Higgs-sector quartic couplings;
- the singlet direction allows a more complicated tunneling path between the symmetric and broken phases.

As a result, the order parameter

\[
\frac{v(T_c)}{T_c}
\]

can exceed unity,

\[
\frac{v(T_c)}{T_c} \gtrsim 1,
\]

which is the usual criterion for avoiding sphaleron washout after the transition. This can occur without requiring an extremely light stop, unlike in the MSSM.

The study finds that for viable choices of the singlet coupling, exotic Yukawa coupling, soft trilinear terms, and \(U(1)'\) charge assignments, the model can produce a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition while also satisfying collider constraints such as limits on the extra \(Z'\) boson and exotic matter.

In short: **the \(U(1)'\)-extended MSSM strengthens the electroweak phase transition through singlet dynamics, exotic-quark thermal effects, and extra gauge interactions, making electroweak baryogenesis more plausible than in the minimal MSSM.**
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise academic abstract explaining whether the minimal supersymmetric standard model with an additional U(1)' can support electroweak baryogenesis through a strong first-order phase transition.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract:**  
The minimal supersymmetric standard model extended by an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry can support electroweak baryogenesis in viable regions of parameter space. The \(U(1)'\) extension typically introduces a Standard Model singlet superfield whose vacuum expectation value generates an effective \(\mu\) term and modifies the finite-temperature Higgs potential. In contrast to the MSSM, where a sufficiently strong first-order electroweak phase transition generally requires a very light stop and is strongly constrained, the \(U(1)'\) model can obtain a strong first-order transition through tree-level effects involving the singlet, additional \(D\)-term contributions, and sizable trilinear soft interactions. These effects can create a barrier between the symmetric and broken phases without relying exclusively on thermal loop corrections, allowing \(v_c/T_c \gtrsim 1\), the usual sphaleron washout criterion. The model may also provide new CP-violating phases relevant for baryon-number generation, although electric dipole moment limits impose important constraints. Compatibility with collider bounds on the extra \(Z'\) boson, Higgs-sector measurements, and supersymmetric particle searches restricts the viable parameter space but does not generically exclude it. Thus, an MSSM+\(U(1)'\) framework can realize electroweak baryogenesis, provided the singlet-sector interactions and soft parameters yield a sufficiently strong first-order phase transition while satisfying current phenomenological constraints.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a short high-energy physics paper abstract on one-loop electroweak phase transitions in a supersymmetric U(1)' model, noting the dependence of neutral Higgs masses on transition strength.
counterfactuals.output: We study the finite-temperature one-loop effective potential of a supersymmetric \(U(1)'\) extension of the Standard Model and analyze the resulting electroweak phase transition. The additional singlet and \(Z'\)-sector interactions modify the Higgs thermal potential and can generate a strongly first-order transition through tree-level and loop-induced effects. We scan the neutral Higgs spectrum and show that the transition strength, characterized by \(v_c/T_c\), is highly sensitive to the CP-even neutral Higgs masses and singlet admixture. In particular, lighter scalar states and enhanced singlet-doublet mixing tend to deepen the broken minimum and increase the order-parameter discontinuity, while heavier neutral Higgs spectra generally weaken the transition. These results indicate that neutral Higgs mass measurements provide a direct probe of electroweak baryogenesis viability in supersymmetric \(U(1)'\) scenarios.

counterfactuals.prompt: In formal scientific language, describe findings on the parameter space for electroweak phase transitions in the MSSM plus an extra U(1)', including how the lightest and heavier neutral Higgs boson masses change as the transition weakens.
counterfactuals.output:
In the MSSM extended by an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry, the electroweak phase transition can be strongly first order over a substantially enlarged region of parameter space relative to the MSSM. This enhancement is primarily associated with new tree-level contributions to the finite-temperature Higgs potential, especially those involving the singlet field that breaks the \(U(1)'\) symmetry and generates an effective \(\mu\) parameter. As a result, a sufficiently strong transition does not require the same degree of reliance on a very light stop as in the MSSM.

Parameter scans typically show that the strength of the transition, often quantified by

\[
\frac{v_c}{T_c},
\]

where \(v_c\) is the Higgs vacuum expectation value at the critical temperature \(T_c\), is controlled by the singlet-Higgs coupling, the soft trilinear parameters, the singlet vacuum expectation value, and the \(U(1)'\) gauge coupling and charge assignments. Strong first-order transitions, satisfying approximately

\[
\frac{v_c}{T_c} \gtrsim 1,
\]

can occur for phenomenologically acceptable Higgs and superpartner spectra.

A characteristic feature of the scan is the correlation between the neutral Higgs spectrum and the strength of the phase transition. As the electroweak phase transition becomes weaker, i.e. as \(v_c/T_c\) decreases, the mass of the lightest neutral Higgs boson tends to increase. Conversely, the heavier neutral Higgs bosons generally become lighter as the transition weakens. Thus, stronger first-order transitions are often associated with a relatively lighter lightest Higgs state and heavier additional neutral Higgs states, while weaker transitions move the spectrum toward a heavier lightest Higgs and reduced masses for the heavier neutral scalars.

This behavior reflects the interplay between the singlet-induced tree-level barrier in the effective potential and the Higgs-sector mass matrix. The same parameters that strengthen the transition, particularly the singlet-Higgs trilinear interactions and associated soft terms, also affect the mixing and mass splitting among the neutral Higgs bosons. Consequently, the model permits a strong electroweak phase transition with Higgs masses beyond the restrictive MSSM expectations, while maintaining a distinctive correlation between transition strength and the neutral Higgs spectrum.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
